findings.pdf_says: FUNCTION  LENGTH  ( argument-1 [ PHYSICAL ] )   -- with FUNCTION, LENGTH and PHYSICAL each UNDERLINED in the printed general format (5.2.6.2: an underlined word is a required word).
findings.markdown_says: ```\nFUNCTION LENGTH ( argument-1 [ PHYSICAL ] )\n```   -- plain fenced code, no underline markup. The same loss occurs in every general format on this batch except 15.58.2 and 15.59.2: 15.51.2 (p905, bare paragraph text), 15.52.2 (p906, inline backticks), 15.53.2 (p907, bare paragraph text), 15.54.2 (p908, fenced code), 15.55.2 (p909, inline backticks), 15.56.2 (p910, inline backticks), 15.57.2 (p911, bare paragraph text).
findings.why_it_matters: The transcription elsewhere DOES carry the standard's underlining as <u>…</u> (97 occurrences, including 15.58.2 `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC</u> ( argument-1 )` on p912 and 15.59.2 `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>MAX</u> ( { argument-1 } … )` on p914 in this very batch). Dropping it on the neighbouring formats loses the required-word marking that 5.2.6.2 makes normative, and the four different renderings used within ten pages (fenced code / inline code / bare paragraph / <u>) make the general-format blocks non-uniform and unreliable to machine-extract. No alternative-selection information is lost on these particular pages, because every uppercase word in each of these formats is underlined in the PDF; hence cosmetic rather than normative.
findings.suggested_repair: Normalize all eight formats to the document's existing convention, e.g. p903: `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>LENGTH</u> ( argument-1 [ <u>PHYSICAL</u> ] )`; p911: `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>LOWER-CASE</u> ( argument-1 [ <u>LOCALE</u> locale-name-1 ] )` (the latter already exists verbatim for UPPER-CASE at 15.79.2).

notes.choice_indicators: No page in this batch prints a choice indicator (a vertical bar just inside a bracket or brace). Every bracket on these pages encloses a single alternative: [ PHYSICAL ] (p903), [ locale-name-1 ] (p905, p906, p907, p908), [ LOCALE locale-name-1 ] (p911).
